heard: A truck-sized space rock skipped off Earth's atmosphere like a stone. On August 10, 1972, the great daylight fireball entered the sky over Utah at 33,000 miles per hour. The object streaked 1,500 kilometers northward, visible in broad daylight across the western United States and Canada. During its pass, the meteoroid dipped to a minimum altitude of just 58 kilometers. Witnesses in Montana reported hearing a startling double sonic boom as the rock rushed overhead. The entire frantic encounter lasted approximately 100 seconds. The dense atmosphere acted like a cosmic ramp, stripping away half the object's mass and warping its orbital tilt from 15 degrees to 7. Having bounced off our sky and escaped back into space, the great daylight fireball was never seen again. in.
